paths.name: complete rational multiplication-map fibres
paths.transformation_type: curve endomorphisms [k], k in {1,2,4,8}, with induced group pushforward

obligations.name: existence and formulas
obligations.evidence: The standard multiplication maps are evaluated with complete affine group arithmetic.

obligations.name: rational kernel and fibres
obligations.evidence: Every one of 1,192 rational points is enumerated for every map and destination column.

obligations.name: subgroup preservation
obligations.evidence: gcd(k,149)=1, and every replayed source row pushes to its exact order-149 destination sum.

obligations.name: quotient rank
obligations.evidence: Each bucket checks dim((span(R)+ker(C))/ker(C))=rank(C(R)) over F_149.

obligations.name: exceptional points
obligations.evidence: Complete group-law enumeration includes infinity; multiplication maps have no omitted rational exceptional branch.

obligations.name: measured advantage
obligations.evidence: Raw sheet rows are removed by the collapse kernel and create no destination-rank gain.

paths.conclusion: Rational sheet multiplicity is real in the cofactor-eight ambient group, but its additional coefficient directions lie in the pushforward kernel.
paths.exploration_boundary: Complete for four multiplication maps, four frozen bases, and all signed arity-three rows on the registered toy curve.

paths.name: P-256 cover or Jacobian pushforward
paths.field_of_definition: must be supplied by a candidate
paths.relevant_subgroup: destination subgroup has prime order n and cofactor one

obligations.name: explicit construction
obligations.evidence: No P-256 cover equation, Jacobian, divisor representation, or executable maps were supplied.

obligations.name: rational multiplication-map fibres
obligations.evidence: For gcd(k,n)=1, [k] is a bijection on the prime-order rational group despite algebraic degree k^2.

obligations.name: kernel-sheet row gain
obligations.evidence: Rows differing only inside a pushforward kernel have identical destination coefficient rows by the exact quotient theorem.
obligations.scope: all linearized relation rows under a group pushforward

obligations.name: inverse recovery and exceptional points
obligations.evidence: Requires explicit formulas and fields for a proposed nontrivial cover.

obligations.name: destination decomposition advantage
obligations.evidence: The experiment does not exclude a cover that makes distinct collapsed decompositions cheaper to find.

obligations.name: paired end-to-end cost
obligations.evidence: No P-256 relation oracle or recovery implementation exists for this family.

paths.conclusion: Algebraic fibre degree cannot be booked as independent P-256 relation rank. A future cover must improve the search for distinct collapsed equations and price the complete maps and recovery.
paths.exploration_boundary: Exact quotient theorem plus P-256 prime-order multiplication-map fact; not a universal search over covers or Jacobians.

controls: Identity map [1] is the no-lift control.
Maps [2], [4], and [8] provide 2, 4, and 8 rational cofactor sheets on the complete toy ambient group.
Scalar-defined high-multiplicity bases and coordinate-defined bases are both included.
Every source sum is pushed forward with exact curve arithmetic and checked against its destination row.
cost_accounting: Measured: fibre scans, every source-row sum, every row pushforward, modular-rank operations, logical coefficient bytes, process telemetry, and artifact bytes.
Exact analytic: P-256 prime-order rational bijectivity and the coefficient-space quotient identity.
Unset: construction and decomposition costs for any nontrivial P-256 cover, inverse recovery, structured degree, relation yield, sparse linear algebra, and full DLP cost.
weakest_open_obligation: Supply an explicit P-256 cover or Jacobian whose algorithm finds distinct collapsed destination decompositions more cheaply, then measure formulas, exceptional sets, inverse recovery, degree, yield, and complete one-target cost.
narrowest_supported_finding: Within the complete registered fibre family, every extra sheet-generated row direction lies in the pushforward kernel; quotient relation rank exactly equals collapsed destination rank.
